title: Fibonacci: Recursion to Space Optimization
contract: Return F(n), where F(0)=0, F(1)=1, and 0 ≤ n ≤ 45. Keep brute-force examples small because its recursion grows exponentially.
brute: emit("Enter a recursive subproblem","n",n);if(n<2)return n;return solve(n-1)+solve(n-2);
optimal: long a=0,b=1;for(int i=0;i<n;i++){long next=a+b;a=b;b=next;emit("Keep only the two preceding states","iteration",i+1,"previous",a,"next",b);}return a;
reasoning: Direct recursion follows the recurrence but recalculates the same F(k) many times.
Memoization would cache each n; tabulation computes states in dependency order.
Only the two previous values are needed, so replace the table with two variables. State clearly whether F(0) or F(1) begins the sequence.
